sections.heading: 1. Micro-breaks
lines: ① Drop your hands and shake them out.
② Open and close your fists 10 times.
③ Gently stretch your wrists both ways.
④ Chair height: elbows about desk height.

sections.heading: 2. Get assessed rather than massaged if…

slides.title:
Forearms still
aching?
slides.heading: Get it checked if you notice

caption:
Five hours of spreadsheets, and by Friday arvo Mr Turtle's forearms feel like lead.

Typing and mousing keep the forearm muscles gently working all day. They rarely get a proper break, so by the end of the week they can feel tight, achy or just plain tired.

Keep your elbows by your sides at about desk height, wrists fairly flat, and the mouse and keyboard close. Every half hour: shake your hands out, open and close your fists 10 times, and gently stretch the wrists. Remedial massage can ease tension and works well alongside these breaks.

Finger tingling, night pain, weakness or swelling are worth assessing first. Our remedial massage therapists at Hybrid Physio can help. Book online via the link in bio.

General information only — not a substitute for an individual assessment.
